citation.title: Evidence for the neoclassical nature of the radial electric field in the edge transport barrier of ASDEX Upgrade
citation.authors: E. Viezzer, T. Pütterich, C. Angioni, A. Bergmann, R. Dux, E. Fable, R.M. McDermott, U. Stroth, E. Wolfrum and the ASDEX Upgrade Team

topic: Edge CXRS poloidal rotation and Er compared with neoclassical models on ASDEX Upgrade
own_question: Is the pedestal Er and the main-ion poloidal rotation consistent with neoclassical theory?
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline active CXRS profiles (impurities in D/H plasmas; He2+ main ions in He plasmas) are compared with NEOART, NEO, HAGIS and an analytic model. Agreement is reported in pedestals with main-ion collisionality of about 1.2-12. There is no Ti nowcasting, BES/ECEI input, KSTAR data or timing analysis.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Background: edge CXRS-derived impurity flows and Er can be interpreted with neoclassical models in AUG H-mode pedestals.
claim_checks.qualification: The scope is a single device and collisional pedestals only. The reported results are rotation and Er, not temperature. The figures were not visually checked.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant: the study uses time-window-averaged offline profiles and has no real-time component.
validation_if_relevant: Model-measurement profile comparison only. There is no predictive split.
forbidden_inferences: That impurity CES Ti equals main-ion Ti in KSTAR.
That the study supports BES/ECEI predictability of Ti.
That the study is relevant to real-time or 10 ms estimation.
That the findings generalize to all pedestals or to low collisionality.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude, or at most cite as optional background on how CXRS impurity measurements relate to main-ion physics. The paper does not inform the nowcasting framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
